narration: One mechanism explains all of it. Learn it once and cold mornings stop being strange.
caption: एक ही तरीक़ा यह सब समझा देता है। समझ लो तो ठंडी सुबहें अजीब नहीं लगतीं।
image_brief: Two metal garden chairs on a terrace at dawn, their upward-facing seats coated white with frost while the vertical backs stay clear, dry terracotta floor beneath.

narration: By the end you will know how a surface goes colder than the air touching it.
caption: अंत तक आप जान जाएँगे कि कोई सतह अपने आसपास की हवा से ठंडी कैसे हो जाती है।
image_brief: A single dark slate roof tile lying alone on a flat stone surface at night, a faint sheen of moisture across its upper face, deep clear sky above.

narration: You will know why those clay pans were filled barely three millimetres deep. That number matters.
caption: आप जानेंगे कि वे मिट्टी के तवे सिर्फ़ तीन मिलीमीटर पानी से क्यों भरे जाते थे।
image_brief: Rows of wide shallow pans inside a walled enclosure, each holding water only a few millimetres deep, the still surfaces mirroring the dark sky above.

narration: You will know why a thin cloth saves a plant, and it is not warmth.
caption: आप जानेंगे कि पतला कपड़ा पौधे को पाले से क्यों बचाता है, और वजह गर्मी नहीं है।
image_brief: A tomato plant draped with a loose white cotton sheet in a vegetable patch at dawn, frost whitening the bare soil all around the covered plant.

narration: And the one number that decides whether ice arrives before sunrise. Just one number.
caption: और वह एक नंबर भी, जो तय करता है कि सूरज उगने से पहले बर्फ़ बनेगी या नहीं।
image_brief: One clay pan at night where a thin plate of ice covers half the water and the other half is still liquid, the boundary between them sharp and straight.

narration: Start with the glow that every warm thing gives off. Including this one, right now.
caption: शुरुआत उस चमक से, जो हर गर्म चीज़ छोड़ती है। अभी इस वक़्त भी।
image_brief: A stack of warm flatbreads on a steel plate in a dim kitchen, steam curling off the top one, the rest of the room unlit.

narration: Everything warmer than absolute zero radiates heat as infrared light. Your skin. The road. Water.
caption: परम शून्य से गर्म हर चीज़ इन्फ़्रारेड के रूप में गर्मी छोड़ती है। त्वचा, सड़क, पानी।
image_brief: A cooling iron griddle on an unlit stove in a dark kitchen, faint heat shimmer rising from the metal, a dull red glow only at the very centre.

narration: At everyday temperatures that glow peaks near ten micrometres. Invisible to eyes. Very real heat.
caption: रोज़मर्रा के तापमान पर यह चमक दस माइक्रोमीटर के पास होती है। आँखों को नहीं दिखती।
image_brief: A single human hair lying across the millimetre divisions of a printed steel ruler on a white sheet, the hair far thinner than one small division.

narration: So every surface is leaking heat outward, constantly. But surfaces also receive the same radiation.
caption: तो हर सतह लगातार गर्मी बाहर बहा रही है। पर सतहें यही विकिरण लेती भी हैं।
image_brief: A large flat granite slab in an empty courtyard at dusk, its surface still faintly warm, dust motes drifting slowly in the last light above it.

narration: What matters is the net. Heat out, minus heat coming back in. That is all.
caption: मायने रखता है शुद्ध हिसाब। बाहर गई गर्मी, घटा वापस आई गर्मी। बस इतना।
image_brief: A two-pan brass balance on a wooden table, one pan holding a small pile of dark stones, the other pan slightly higher, even indoor light.

narration: Point a plate at a warm wall. The wall glows back almost exactly as hard.
caption: एक प्लेट को गर्म दीवार की तरफ़ करो। दीवार लगभग उतनी ही गर्मी वापस देती है।
image_brief: A white ceramic plate propped upright half a metre from a sunlit brick wall in a narrow alley, warm light filling the gap between the two.

narration: Net flow near zero. The plate stays at wall temperature. Nothing dramatic happens. Ever.
caption: शुद्ध बहाव लगभग शून्य। प्लेट दीवार के तापमान पर रहती है। कुछ नहीं होता।
image_brief: The same ceramic plate and brick wall at night, both dull grey and indistinguishable in tone, still air, no light source visible in the alley.

narration: Now turn the plate to face straight up at a clear night sky. What glows back?
caption: अब प्लेट को साफ़ रात के आसमान की तरफ़ सीधा ऊपर करो। अब वापस क्या चमकेगा?
image_brief: A white ceramic plate lying face up on a wooden stool in the middle of a dark open yard, the entire clear starry sky open above it.

narration: The air does glow back. But only at the wavelengths its molecules can absorb and emit.
caption: हवा वापस चमकती तो है। पर सिर्फ़ उन तरंगों पर जिन्हें उसके अणु सोख सकते हैं।
image_brief: A hazy night sky over a still lake, faint bands of moisture hanging low over the water, the stars near the horizon dimmed and smeared.

narration: Water vapour handles a wide band. Carbon dioxide handles another. Together they cover most of it.
caption: जलवाष्प एक चौड़ी पट्टी सोखती है, कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड दूसरी। मिलकर ज़्यादातर ढक लेती हैं।
image_brief: A jar of water and a sealed glass flask of faintly clouded gas standing side by side on a shelf, a bright lamp behind them throwing both shadows forward.
